title: E2E observability spec for analytics ingest pipeline
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: Define, implement, and validate end-to-end observability for the analytics ingestion pipeline that powers Console usage dashboards. This ticket covers SLIs/SLOs, distributed tracing propagation, sampling and structured logging conventions, alerting rules, and a set of dashboards and runbooks for on-call and product owners.

Background: Our current analytics pipeline (console events -> Kafka -> Flink processors -> materialized ClickHouse tables -> Console dashboards) has intermittent blind spots: dropped events during spikes, long tail latency in materialized views after deploys, and limited traceability across the streaming join stages. Existing tickets focused on metrics instrumentation and dashboard contract work, but we lack a single end-to-end spec and concrete SLI definitions to tie alerts to customer impact.

Scope:
- Define E2E SLIs (ingest success rate, event-to-row 95/99p latency, per-tenant ingestion lag, pipeline backpressure indicators) and explicit SLO targets for each SLI.
- Add tracing headers propagation across producers, Kafka topics, Flink jobs, and the materializer; ensure traces link to dashboard rows for sampled requests.
- Establish structured logging schema for ingestion microservices and Flink sinks, with consistent event_id, tenant_id, trace_id, and processing_stage fields.
- Design dashboards: ingest health overview, per-tenant latency heatmap, transient drop detection, and consumer lag & backlog view.
- Create alerting rules mapped to SLO burn rate and runbooks with remediation steps and rollback guidance.
- Deliver integration tests and a small sampling harness to validate trace propagation and SLI computations in staging.

Out of scope: full retention/long-term analytics storage policy, dashboard UX polishing, and non-console product pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Documented SLIs and SLO targets published in Confluence and linked in ticket
Tracing headers successfully propagated end-to-end in staging with sample traces linking producer -> Flink -> materializer
Structured logging schema deployed for ingestion service and Flink sinks and consumed by logging pipeline
Dashboards created in Grafana: ingest-overview, tenant-latency-heatmap, consumer-lag; perf validated against synthetic traffic
Alert rules configured for high drop rate, 99p event-to-row latency breach, and sustained backlog growth with runbooks
Automated integration test demonstrates synthetic event flow and validates SLI calculation within a 5% margin
